page: Microsoft Azure D96nlds_v6 is an x86_64 server instance powered by dedicated Intel processors running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The virtual machine provides 96 dedicated vCPUs alongside 192.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 2.0 GB of memory per core. The configuration includes 5670 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage and supports Premium Storage configurations, but includes zero graphics processing units and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Categorized as a network-optimized, low-memory variant within Azure's D-family, the instance trades standard general-purpose memory density for concentrated compute and extensive fast scratch storage. The dense 96-core count paired with 5670 GB of direct NVMe ephemeral storage targets high I/O throughput scenarios without paying for excessive, unutilized memory capacity. Cost efficiency stems from this constrained memory footprint, which lowers total resource overhead relative to standard 1:4 memory configurations while retaining full compute capacity.

Workloads best aligned with the D96nlds_v6 profile include compute-bound data processing pipelines, distributed batch computations, build and continuous integration environments, network routing appliances, and high-performance ephemeral databases requiring substantial scratch disk space alongside intensive multi-threaded processing.
description: Microsoft Azure D96nlds_v6 is a high-density, compute-oriented x86_64 instance featuring 96 dedicated Intel vCPUs and 192.0 GB of memory, yielding a 1:2 compute-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the platform integrates 5670 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and supports Premium Storage capabilities, with no onboard GPUs. As a low-memory, network-optimized variant within the broader D-series family, it reduces memory overhead relative to standard general-purpose instances, improving resource cost efficiency for compute-heavy applications. The substantial local disk capacity accommodates massive temporary datasets and intensive local disk operations. The instance is well-suited for high-throughput batch compute, parallel compiling, network processing nodes, and database workloads requiring high parallel CPU throughput paired with fast local scratch volumes.
